subject: Business
title: Capital Gains Tax: Selling Winners
description: Learn Capital Gains Tax: Selling Winners in one minute.

hook.text: You sell a stock for $10,000 profit. Uncle Sam takes $1,500 — or $3,700, depending on how long you held it.

buildup.text: Capital gains tax applies to profits from selling investments. Long-term (held 1+ year) rates are lower than short-term.

discovery.text: Short-term gains are taxed as ordinary income (up to 37%). Long-term gains top out at 20% for most investors.

twist.text: Tax-loss harvesting lets you sell losers to offset gains, reducing your tax bill while maintaining your portfolio.

climax.text: Billionaires 'buy, borrow, die': hold assets (no tax), borrow against them (no income), heirs inherit (stepped-up basis).

punchline.text: It's not what you earn. It's what you keep after taxes.

quiz.question: Why are long-term capital gains taxed at a lower rate?
options: To incentivize holding investments for longer periods rather than frequent trading
Because long-term investments are always riskier
The government doesn't track long-term gains

details.summary: Capital gains tax applies when you sell an investment for more than you paid. Short-term gains on assets held under a year are taxed at ordinary income rates, while long-term gains on assets held over a year receive preferential lower tax rates.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding capital gains timing can save thousands in taxes. Holding investments beyond one year to qualify for long-term rates is one of the simplest tax optimization strategies available to individual investors.
takeaways: Short-term capital gains are taxed at your regular income tax rate
Long-term gains held over one year receive lower preferential tax rates
Tax-loss harvesting can offset gains to reduce your overall tax bill

faq.question: What is tax-loss harvesting and how does it work?
faq.answer: Selling investments at a loss to offset capital gains from winners. If your losses exceed gains, you can deduct up to 3,000 dollars against ordinary income annually. Remaining losses carry forward to future years. The wash sale rule prevents repurchasing the same security within 30 days.

faq.question: Do you pay capital gains on investments in retirement accounts?
faq.answer: No. Investments in traditional IRAs and 401(k)s grow tax-deferred. You pay ordinary income tax on withdrawals instead. Roth accounts grow tax-free and qualified withdrawals are completely untaxed, making them ideal for high-growth investments.
